title: Kernel gating and attention deopt recovery: playbook, hardening, and action items
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a sustained high-concurrency capacity event on 2026-02-08 we observed repeated attention kernel deoptimizations and functional kernel gating that caused a ~2.3x increase in median token latency and a 30% drop in P50 throughput for several production models. This ticket captures the recovery playbook we used during the incident, the short-term mitigations, and a prioritized set of follow-up engineering tasks to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-08 11:12 UTC: First increase in tail latency alerted on runtime-p95; 11:18: PagerDuty escalated. 11:20–11:40: Hotfix 1 rolled (disable speculative probe path) reduced error rate but not latency. 11:45: Observed kernel switchbacks between fused_attn_v2 and scalar_attn_deopt when sequence lengths spiked; 12:05: Canary of a kernel gating threshold bumped to force fused_attn_v2 selection, improved p50 but p95 remained high. 13:30: Deployed KV-cache-warmup smoothing (short-term), restored normal throughput by 14:05. 14:30: Incident declared resolved; began root-cause analysis and follow-ups.
root_cause: Root cause was an interaction between the scheduler's speculative probing window and our kernel ranking heuristic. Under a burst of mixed sequence lengths, the probe logic briefly preferred a fallback scalar attention kernel (identified as 'scalar_attn_deopt') for a subset of workers. That kernel has worse throughput characteristics at scale and caused queueing on GPU workers which amplified scheduler probes and triggered additional misrouting. Contributing factors: (1) recent heuristic change that tightened quantization-safe thresholds; (2) lack of damping on kernel preference flips; (3) insufficient observability for per-worker kernel selection churn.
short_term_mitigations: Rolled back heuristic tightening change (revert PR #4382) to restore previous kernel-ranking weights
Applied probe-window damping to scheduler (hotfix deployment runtime-1.24-hf1) to reduce oscillation frequency
Enabled KV-cache warmup smoothing to reduce cold-start bursts and reduce mixed-sequence amplification
action_items: AH-1: Implement kernel-selection hysteresis (engine) — introduce time-based gating so a worker must run a kernel for >= N seconds before flipping (owner: Marco, est 3)
AH-2: Add per-worker kernel churn metrics and alerting to Grafana (owner: SRE team, est 2)
AH-3: Rework probe-window algorithm to incorporate backlog and worker utilization (owner: Scheduling squad, est 5)
AH-4: Add regression test harness for mixed sequence-length bursts that asserts no >1.5x p50 degradation across candidate kernels (owner: QA, est 3)
AH-5: Document an incident runbook chapter for kernel-deopt events with escalation steps and safe rollback checklist (owner: DevEx, est 2)
AH-6: Profile scalar_attn_deopt and create micro-optimizations or replacement kernels if needed (owner: Applied ML / Runtime, est 8)
AH-7: Schedule a cross-team review of recent kernel ranking changes before merge (owner: Eng Managers, est 1)
AH-8: Add automated canary that runs a synthetic mixed-length workload after scheduler heuristic changes (owner: Canary infra, est 3)
AH-9: Evaluate introducing a soft-capacity discriminator so probes avoid workers near a utilization inflection point (owner: Scheduling squad, est 4)
AH-10: Post-incident customer impact review and targeted outreach for top-10 affected namespaces (owner: CS/Success, due 2026-02-25)

decision_log: Decision: revert heuristic tightening (PR #4382) as immediate rollback; follow with hysteresis + probe-damping rather than hard thresholds. Rationale: hysteresis reduces flip-flops without reducing kernel diversity for edge cases.
qa_acceptance_criteria: 1) No >1.2x p50 regression on synthetic mixed workload after hysteresis; 2) kernel_churn_rate alert fires in test cluster when artificially stimulated; 3) canary run shows stable P95 under 150% of baseline concurrency.
notes: This ticket bundles the operational playbook and engineering follow-ups. Keep stakeholders notified in #incidents and update the Confluence page with playbook steps as actions are completed. Prioritize customer outreach once AH-10 owner confirms affected namespaces list.
